headline: Hawkish Fed pivot and Gulf tensions test an earnings-fueled rally
body: The dominant story this week is a rapid repricing of Fed expectations: after Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks stressing that inflation is 'still too high,' fed funds futures now imply roughly a two-thirds chance of a rate hike at the September meeting, a sharp reversal from cut-leaning odds just a week ago. That shift has pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest level since late 2023, near 4.8%, with traders also citing heavy AI-related corporate debt issuance crowding out demand for governments. Layered on top is renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz, which pressured futures overnight before a report of record oil-tanker transit through the strait calmed some of the worst supply fears, alongside a soft ADP jobs print, letting crude and yields ease back toward flat into the US open.

Earnings are cutting both ways. Broadcom beat on revenue and EPS, with semiconductor sales more than tripling, yet shares still fell roughly 5% after fourth-quarter guidance landed just short of estimates — a reminder that AI-infrastructure names are being priced for perfection. Software and security names such as Salesforce, CrowdStrike and Okta fared better, trading higher on solid results. Retail chatter mirrors that split: WallStreetBets mention volume is clustering around Broadcom, Nvidia and the AI megacaps following the print, while Stocktwits activity leans toward speculative names like TG Therapeutics on buyout chatter and Robinhood on product-diversification optimism. The social-sentiment signal reads as idiosyncratic rather than directional today, so this read leans more on price action and the Fed/yield story than on any clear retail consensus.
